title: Choosing bean varieties
subtitle: Broad, runner, and French beans: what to grow for yield, flavour, and season
excerpt: UK gardens can grow broad beans (autumn or spring sowing), runner beans (summer climbers), and French beans (dwarf or climbing). Each occupies a different season and space in the plot. This guide covers reliable variety choices for each type.
sourceNotes: RHS bean variety guide (rhs.org.uk). USDA cooperative extension notes on bean variety selection, public domain. RHS AGM award lists, public domain.

glossaryTerms.definition: A runner bean or French bean variety bred to have minimal or no fibrous string running along the pod seam. Traditional runner bean varieties have a noticeable string that must be removed before cooking; stringless types can be cooked without this step. Stringless runner bean varieties include Lady Di, Polestar, and Enorma. All modern French beans are effectively stringless.

content.text: The three UK garden bean types fill different slots in the growing season. Broad beans are the earliest: sown in autumn or spring and harvested in May to July. Runner beans occupy a midsummer slot, producing from July to October. French beans are the most flexible: faster than runners, suited to containers, and available as dwarf or climbing types.

Aquadulce Claudia is the standard autumn sowing variety; it is hardy enough to overwinter outside in most of the UK and crops in May. Bunyards Exhibition and Crimson Flowered are traditional spring-sown varieties with excellent flavour. The Sutton is a dwarf variety reaching 30 to 45 cm, suitable for exposed or windy sites. Witkiem Manita and Express are reliable for spring sowing with a shorter days-to-harvest.
Lady Di is one of the best

runner bean varieties and holds an Award of Garden Merit. Enorma is a classic long-podded show variety with good flavour. Polestar is stringless with very high yields. Scarlet Emperor is the most widely available standard variety. For a short space, Hestia is a dwarf non-climbing runner bean reaching 45 cm that can be grown in containers.

Dwarf: The Prince (flat-podded, excellent flavour, Award of Garden Merit), Tendergreen (pencil-podded, productive), Safari (disease-resistant, reliable). Climbing: Cobra (pencil-podded, long season, reliable), Fasold (pencil-podded, good yields over a long period). For coloured varieties: Purple Teepee (dwarf, purple pods that turn green on cooking, good visual interest in the plot). Borlotti types (Lingua di Fuoco) are grown for drying or semi-dried eating; pods are picked when speckled and shell from the pod.
